summary: Internet service provider Transworld Associates has said repair work on an affected international submarine cable is expected to be completed by December 6, with users likely to experience slower internet speeds during peak hours until the work is finished.

Internet monitoring organisation NetBlocks had also reported a decline in connectivity in Pakistan, saying the incident was consistent with a fault in the SMW5 international subsea cable system.

summary: Countries agreed on Saturday to open a path towards finding an international agreement on regulating lethal autonomous weapons systems, though campaigners seeking to stop so-called killer robots were disappointed by the “watered-down” outcome.

The 128 countries party to the CCW “agreed to launch the elaboration of an international instrument on lethal autonomous weapons systems, which should be conducted over the next two years”, conference president Julien Thoni told reporters afterwards.
While a majority of states went in favour of a legally binding agreement, countries that have the technology, including the United States and Russia, are reluctant to have their hands tied.

summary: KARACHI: The issue of an alarming rise in dog-bite cases echoed in the Sindh Assembly on Friday, with the government claiming that the process of catching stray dogs for vaccination is under way across the province.

Local Government Minister Syed Nasir Hussain Shah said that considerable work had been done on stray dogs, but more steps were needed. “The process of catching stray dogs, vaccinating them and releasing them again is under way in different areas of the province,” he added.
The minister said that a pilot project of the digital labour inspection system was under way in Karachi, and the labour department’s manual system was gradually being shifted online.

stories.title: Magistrate indicts anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan for cyberterrorism
summary: KARACHI: A judicial magistrate (East) on Friday framed charges against anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan in a case pertaining to cyberterrorism and the alleged dissemination of anti-state, false and defamatory content on his official social media accounts.

Last month, Mr Hassan was arrested by National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) at his home in Lahore in connection with a case registered in Karachi under multiple provisions of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca).

The NCCIA had registered a case against Mr Hassan for offences under Sections 9 (glorification of an offence), 10 (cyberterrorism), 20 (offences against dignity of a natural person), 24 (cyberstalking) and 26-A (punishment for false and fake information) of Peca.
